title: Proposed Proof of the Higher-Dimensional Kakeya Conjecture (n ≥ 4)
whyItMatters: Extends the landmark 2025 3D Kakeya breakthrough to all higher Euclidean dimensions n ≥ 4—currently under rigorous inspection by harmonic analysts.
summary: Less than 20 months after Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl proved the 3-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, OpenAI announced on October 26, 2026 an AI-derived proof tackling the general higher-dimensional Kakeya conjecture (n ≥ 4) as part of its trio of math, CS, and physics discoveries. If validated, it completes the Hausdorff-dimension Kakeya conjecture across all Euclidean dimensions.
technicalHighlights: Targets the full n ≥ 4 dimensional generalization of Besicovitch/Kakeya set Hausdorff dimension.
Builds directly in the intellectual wake of Wang and Zahl's February 2025 3D breakthrough.
Released to academic harmonic analysts for independent line-by-line refereeing.
caveats: Not yet independently peer-reviewed or universally accepted; harmonic analysts are closely examining the high-dimensional induction steps for potential hidden gaps.

scoreRationale.foundational: Completing the Kakeya dimension conjecture in all dimensions would resolve a century-old centerpiece of harmonic analysis.
scoreRationale.ripple: Strong implications for high-dimensional Fourier restriction, Bochner–Riesz, and oscillatory integral theory.
scoreRationale.verification: Held back pending independent expert verification and formalization checks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Proposed less than two years after the 3D breakthrough—an astonishing compression of expected timelines.
